title: Profiled compile verdict: projected rule unconditionally, DS14 companion rule only along certified sequences
statement: On the conditionally centered class (d_psi = d_lambda = 1): (a) the projected efficient-score interval rule is the only CURRENTLY ESTABLISHED unconditional compile path in the registered theory, not a mathematical uniqueness theorem. By the DS16 funnel, every asymptotically value-convergent free-optimizer sequence is nuisance-degenerate with an unstable companion slope, so refusal to compile a free profiled terminal state remains the safe default. (b) DS14 supplies a sequence-conditional companion-rule theorem: for exchange-stable sequences satisfying the law assumptions (M1)/(M4) and eventually uniform (M2)/(M3)/(M5), or the audited merged variant, its companion efficient-Voronoi rules geometrize and have population-stationary subsequential limits. One finite fit passing exchange stability plus measured mass, conditioning, and separation checks is only a diagnostic candidate; it does not establish those sequence hypotheses or a population guarantee. DS16 prices every finite state with lambda_min(I_hat) >= kappa pathwise, so report the observable finite gap v_hat_K - Phi_hat_s. The population delta(kappa) is existential and cannot be numerically reported without a law-specific lower bound. (c) certificate-branch inhabitation, constrained-solver existence, and attainment of the constrained population value remain OPEN-DS-STABLE-BASINS / OP7. The projected rule attains v_K only in the distinct formulation with nuisance information supplied externally or unbinned.
assumptions: class (L)+(S), d_psi = d_lambda = 1, equal weights, exact scores; the conditional path's asymptotic guarantee is DS14's and inherits (M1)-(M5), or the merged variant, along a sequence
a per-fit measured triple plus exact exchange stability is diagnostic only and is not a finite-sample population certificate
beyond the class (non-centered laws): measured only (mix3 keeps lambda_min = Theta(1) at terminal states); OP29's mathematical branches remain open
